anya: Heads-up — saw a weird queue imbalance on the continuous-batcher this AM. Short requests are getting pushed back while a few long sequences hold most of the batch slots. KV hit rate for low-latency tenants dipped too. Anyone else seeing this?

liam: saw some alerts. p99 latency jumped ~2x for API tier A around 09:12 UTC. Do you have profiler output? :thinking:

anya: pasting the quick profiler snippet I grabbed from the service box (trimmed):
```
[cont-batcher] window=30s avg_batch_size=17.8
short_reqs_pct=71.2 long_reqs_pct=6.5 (heavy-tail)
avg_tokens_per_req=128
KV_global_hit=0.62 (baseline ~0.87 last week)
kernel_fallbacks=45/min (fused-attn -> generic)
p99_latency_ms=842 (baseline 350)
```

sam: interesting — kernel fallback number stands out. If kernel selector chooses slower path for long sequences it can increase time each request occupies batch slot which amplifies queue imbalance. Could be an interaction between seq-length-based kernel choice and our batch formation heuristics.

noah: +1. Also noticed token_budget_target for some tenants doubled after the rollback of the previous tuning PR — that makes long sequences consume more of the token-credit pool per tenant. Noticed config: `token_budget_target=400` for tenant:ai-saas while default is 200.

liam: do we have a timeline correlation between token_budget_target change and kernel selector regression? Might be two independent regressions that amplify each other.

anya: timeline: 08:50 deploy changed token budget defaults (rollout flagged), 09:00 kernel selector tweak rolled out (attempt to favor memory-saver kernel for long seqs). 09:05 we started seeing higher fallback rate to generic kernel on the new instances — looks like the memory-saver path missed an AVX512 kernel and fell back.

sam: concrete mitigations we can try quickly: 1) short-fast-path: reserve some batch slots or a small queue for sequences <= 32 tokens so they don't compete with long seqs; 2) tenant caps: per-tenant inflight token cap so one tenant can't monopolize; 3) kernel selector guard: if fallback rate > X then pin to last-known-good kernel.

liam: for short-fast-path we can implement an age-biased queue policy: prioritize items with low token_remaining and low queue_age. That should keep small requests fast without starving older long requests.

noah: we should also avoid hard caps that underutilize GPUs. Proposal: token credits per tenant with periodic refill but allow a small burst buffer so latency-sensitive tenants can spike. Example: `credits=200 refill=10/s burst=50`.

anya: added a quick reproduce script on staging to validate:
```bash
# simulate mixed load
python tools/sim_load.py --short qps=150 seq_len=12 --long qps=5 seq_len=1024 --tenants=3
# collect /debug/cont-batcher/stats
```

liam: ran it — with current algo we see avg_batch=20 but effective concurrency dominated by 6 long reqs, short p50 stays ok but p95/p99 for short spikes.

sam: small A/B test plan: (A) enable short-fast-path (slot reservation 8%) (B) enable tenant token credits (200/10s). Run for 30m windows and compare KV hit, short p99, GPU utilization.

noah: one more note: KV cache behavior is impacted because long sequences produce many unique prefixes and push out useful prefixes for short requests. Short-fast-path + prefilling KV for short-tenants (predictive prefetch of common small-prefixes) could recover hit rate.

liam: good point. Also instrument kernel selector to emit per-model kernel-choice histograms by seq_len bucket (0-32,33-128,129-512,512+). That will help detect mis-routes.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: cont-batcher/short-fast-path-experiment -> canary on staging at 1812350500, prod after A/B results.

anya: I'll run the A/B and dump profilers. If we see kernel fallback still high we'll rollback the selector tweak and keep token_budget_target change scoped.

sam: thanks. If A/B shows short p99 improvement with <5% loss in throughput we should keep it. If it regresses GPU efficiency >10% then iterate on slot sizing and burst parameters.

liam: great. tagging @sre for observability alerts and @ml-infra for kernel selector follow-up.

anya: attaching one-line notes after first 10m of staging: short p99 improved 38%, KV_hit up 12pp, GPU util -3%. Will post full numbers after full run. :thumbsup:
